target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D036) defines the fiscal year convention (52/53 weeks ending near Oct 31) and states that 2023 was a 52-week year. The 2024 filing splits this topic: D043 defines the general convention (similar to 2023 D036), while D003 specifically discusses the 2024 vs 2023 comparison (53-week vs 52-week) and the impact of the extra week. D003 contains specific comparative data not present in D043, and D043 contains the general policy definition present in D036. Both are needed to cover the fiscal year presentation topic completely.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by favorable movements including lower period charges from sell-through of previously reserved inventory, lower non-accelerator reserves, lower excess capacity charges, and benefits from CHIPS Act government incentives.
comparisons.comparison: The target disclosure explains that the fiscal year 2024 was a 53-week year, which structurally resulted in higher gross margin dollars due to the additional week of revenue and expenses. In contrast, Intel's disclosure focuses on operational drivers of gross margin variance, specifically noting that unfavorable impacts were offset by favorable movements such as lower period charges from selling previously reserved inventory and CHIPS Act incentives. While both discuss gross margin outcomes in 2024, the target attributes part of the financial result to calendar length (53 weeks), whereas Intel attributes its gross margin stability/variation to specific operational cost adjustments and government incentives rather than calendar duration.

sentences.text: The additional week in the first quarter of fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue, gross margin dollars, research and development expense, and selling general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2024, compared to the corresponding prior year fiscal period.

These 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by certain favorable gross margin movements in 2024, including lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower non-accelerator reserves taken, lower period charges related to excess capacity charges, and a benefit recognized for government incentives received under the CHIPS Act.
